The Standard Cannot Move
Inspired by James 2:1, Proverbs 21:3 & Micah 6:8

There is a question God eventually places before every heart:

Do you love truth—or only the truth that agrees with you?

Conviction is easy when it costs us nothing.

It is easy to recognize wrongdoing in someone we already distrust. Easy to demand accountability when another person’s hands are dirty. Easy to speak boldly about justice when justice requires nothing from us.

But the true measure of integrity comes when truth knocks on our own door.

When it concerns someone we love.
Someone we admire.
Someone we defended.
Someone from our family, church, circle—or side.

Suddenly, the standard begins to move.

We make excuses.
We explain away what we once condemned.
We question evidence we would have accepted from anyone else.

And somewhere along the way, loyalty becomes more important than truth.

But God does not judge with shifting scales.

He does not have one standard for the stranger and another for the friend.

Influence does not intimidate Him.
Money cannot purchase His favor.
Popularity cannot rewrite His truth.
Family connections cannot change what He sees.

Our affection for someone does not make wrong become right.

The standard cannot move simply because applying it has become uncomfortable.

Sometimes integrity requires changing our opinion.

Sometimes obedience means refusing to defend what should not be defended.

Sometimes loving someone means refusing to participate in their deception.

And sometimes following God means standing alone while others choose allegiance over truth.

Jesus never called us to protect appearances.

He called us to walk in the light.

That does not mean believing every accusation or spreading rumors. God is a God of truth and justice.

We seek facts.
We use discernment.
We refuse gossip and mob judgment.

But once truth becomes clear, we do not bend it to preserve our comfort.

Truth does not need our permission to remain true.

Perhaps one of the greatest tests of spiritual maturity is being willing to pray:

“Lord, show me the truth—not the answer I want.”

Can I love someone without calling darkness light?

Can I forgive without pretending there was no wrongdoing?

Can I show mercy without abandoning justice?

Can I stand for what is right when it may cost me relationships, approval, or belonging?

God is not asking us which side we are on.

He is asking whether we are willing to stand on His.

The side of truth.
Justice.
Mercy.
Righteousness.

The side that refuses favoritism, protects the vulnerable, and will not exchange conviction for acceptance.

The world will constantly invite us to choose teams.

But followers of Christ were never called to worship teams.

We were called to follow Truth Himself.

So when loyalty and righteousness pull in opposite directions, remember:

Principles that disappear under pressure were never really principles.

And faith that only stands when standing is easy has not yet learned the strength of surrender.

Lord,

Give us hearts that cannot be bought by approval and eyes willing to see what is true.

Give us wisdom to separate evidence from rumor, justice from vengeance, and loyalty from idolatry.

Teach us to defend the innocent, seek truth without fear, and extend mercy without abandoning righteousness.

And when truth costs us something, give us the courage to choose You anyway.

Because when every opinion fades, every reputation disappears, and every earthly allegiance is gone—

Your truth will still be standing.

And so should we.

Amen. 📜🙏

⚡ Cyberattack volume has risen sharply during the summer
💰 Ransomware victims surged — including +87% in July and nearly +100% in August year-over-year

💧 100+ U.S. water/wastewater systems targeted

📡 Telecommunications and internet infrastructure

And then there are the ZERO-DAY stories. They’ve become a recurring feature of the news cycle.

Zero-day.
Critical infrastructure.

Foreign hackers.

Network vulnerabilities.

The public has been hearing these concepts repeatedly.

Maybe that’s simply because the threat environment really is getting worse.
